name: The Argan of the Orto Botanico

location.address: Orto Botanico di Cagliari, Viale Sant'Ignazio da Laconi 1, Cagliari

access: Paid entry, euro 4 (reduced/free for children under 6, over 65s, disabled visitors and school groups). Open Monday to Saturday, closed Sundays and some public holidays. Same garden and terms as cag_011-013.
transport: In central Cagliari, same site as cag_011-013 (the Moreton Bay Fig, Ombu and Dragon Tree of the Orto Botanico); about a 15 minute walk from the Giardini Pubblici cluster (cag_001-003).
verify_notes: Alive/current: Orto Botanico di Cagliari is confirmed open and operating (sites.unica.it/hbk lists current opening hours, guided visits and ticket prices, checked Sept 2026, prices and hours consistent with cag_011-013's note already on file). Species/rarity: two independent sources both describe this as the only Argania sideroxylon/spinosa specimen in an Italian (and probably European) botanical garden -- apgi.it (Associazione Parchi e Giardini Italiani): 'argan (Argania sideroxylon), unico negli orti botanici italiani'; luoghi.italianbotanicalheritage.com (Italian Botanical Heritage): 'a wondrous specimen of Argania sideroxylon, endemic of Morocco (probably the only one growing in Italian and European Botanical Gardens)'. A third, independent academic source (ricerca.uniba.it, a University of Bari research record on Argania spinosa in Puglia) states as background: 'in Italia l'unico dato riguardante la presenza di piante di A. spinosa fa riferimento ad un esemplare situato nell'orto botanico di Cagliari' (in Italy the only documented A. spinosa specimen is the one at the Cagliari botanical garden). Three independent sources agreeing clears the two-source bar comfortably. Why remarkable/worth the visit: this is the reason to see it, not age or size, but rarity. It is, per two independent horticultural sources, the only argan tree in any Italian or European botanical garden, a species normally confined to semi-arid Morocco and grown almost nowhere else in Europe. No age, girth or planting date found in any source; unlike cag_011-013, no source names this specimen as part of the garden's 1866 founding-era planting, so that bridge is NOT made here (the founding-era age band used for cag_011-013 does not transfer to this tree without its own source). age_estimate and girth left empty rather than guessed; a future visitor or gardener could supply a girth. Location: garden-level precision only, same as cag_011-013 (no source gives an exact bed or path location within the 5-hectare garden); coordinates placed near the garden centre as a placeholder consistent with the other three entries, flagged approximate. Species-match note for a future photo: Argania sideroxylon has small, leathery, oval grey-green leaves and thorny branches, distinct from the broad-leaved fig, the swollen-trunked ombu and the sword-leaved dragon tree already mapped in the same garden, so it will not be confused with them.
